questions.question: When driving, how should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place them on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic.
When vehicles are too close to one another.

questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers change lanes or turn too quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue while driving include difficulty focusing, repeated yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane. The ability to focus is the opposite of a fatigue sign.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Any glad hand can connect to any other glad hand.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Connect only matching glad hands together. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is typically used for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper generally list?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the planned route.

questions.explanation: Shippers must list an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. There are a few exceptions to this rule.

questions.question: While seated at the steering wheel, where should shipping papers be kept?

options.text: Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch in the driver's side door or in another location you can easily reach while wearing your seat belt. The papers must be easily visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: If you see a large box in your lane ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Don't worry because another vehicle will hit it first.
Swerve into another lane of traffic.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see objects in your lane. Even a light cardboard box could contain heavy or hard items that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond to an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: basic descriptions and technical names of the materials; immediate health hazards; risks of fire or explosion; precautions for accidents; methods for handling fires; methods for handling spills or leaks; and preliminary first aid measures.

questions.question: A vehicle should be equipped with all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, such as flares.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry a fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless it has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as triangles or flares. A spotlight is not required.

questions.question: What may rust around wheel nuts indicate?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate they are loose. Check if the nuts are tight whenever you see rust in that area.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: A truck driver is driving too fast.
The driver in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
A truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: After you finish a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brake lines on all trailers. You should hear escaping air. Close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, you should NOT:

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.explanation: If a trailer starts to jackknife, release the brakes and let the trailer wheels regain grip on the road. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because it will make the skid worse. Brakes are what caused the wheels to lock up in the first place.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, you should:
questions.explanation: If you cannot tell if your vehicle will fit under a bridge or other overhead object, slow down and find a different route.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, it is especially important that you:

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for your vehicle.
Wait for other drivers to wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is enough gap for you to move safely.

questions.question: Escape ramps are:

options.text: Ramps to exit the interstate quickly.
Ramps connecting four-lane and two-lane highways.
Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
Ramps that only trucks can use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill grades to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have a long bed of loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be checked for:

options.text: Whether they are connected to the battery.
The proper amount of brake fluid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: The steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with one hand so you can eat and drink.
Held with one hand at a time, switching hands.

questions.explanation: To control your vehicle properly, hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while transporting explosives, you may warn other drivers with:

options.text: Standing on the road and waving your arms.
Keeping the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, warn other drivers using reflective triangles or electric lights. Do not use flares or other open flame signals because they could start a fire.

questions.question: After a trailer starts to turn while you are backing, you should:

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Change the direction of the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel farther in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change the direction of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the steering wheel the opposite way to follow the trailer.
